advances: This rules out a first-order law based only on added masses and fiberwise weak limits. It concerns the global maximum of the actual source.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Use the seven-fiber theorem with $w=a=\tau V$, where $V$ is the common core simplex volume. In the first family take all three added bodies to be the homothet of $T$ about its centroid $g$ with ratio $\tau^{1/d}$. In the second take a fixed centrally symmetric convex body about $g$, scaled there to volume $\tau V$, for each addition. For all sufficiently small $\tau$ these bodies lie in $T$ and meet both mass bounds. The core fibers are identical and constant. The added bodies in each family shrink to $g$, so their normalized laws tend weakly to $\delta_g$, while their masses are equal throughout. The seven-fiber result gives the unique maximum at $((0,0),g)$ in each case, and its exact normalization gives the displayed fractions. Differentiate them at zero.

For extra integer dimensions take the product with $[0,1]^{n-2}$. The integer fibers consist of the binary copies of the original seven, with their original shapes and masses. Restriction of any containing halfspace to the selected binary copy gives at least its own raw depth. Conversely any original containing cap extends to a cap excluding all other copies by adding a sufficiently large negative multiple of an affine function that vanishes at the selected binary vertex and is positive at every other vertex. The original margin is uniformly bounded on the compact source, and the finite positive gap makes this extension exact. Thus the raw depth at each point equals that in its own copy. Total volume is multiplied by the number of copies, proving the asserted normalized factors.
statement:
In every $n,d\ge2$ there are two families of actual compact mixed-integer convex sources with the same integer support, the same fiber volumes for each sufficiently small $\tau>0$, and the same weak limits of the normalized laws on every fiber, whose normalized maximum depths have different first-order coefficients in $\tau$. For $n=2$ their normalized maxima are exactly
$$
\frac{\Gamma_d+(1+2\Gamma_d)\tau}{4+3\tau},
\qquad
\frac{\Gamma_d+2\tau}{4+3\tau},
\qquad
\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.
$$
The right derivative of the second minus that of the first is $(1-2\Gamma_d)/4>0$. For $n>2$ both normalized maxima and the derivative difference are multiplied by $2^{-(n-2)}$.
title: Equal shell masses and weak limits with different first-order global depths
